sections.h2: Pumps: about half of the chip-tampering cases were in Uttar Pradesh

chart.title: Uttar Pradesh had 51 of the 101 cases the oil ministry reported
chart.sub: Cases of chips or other high-tech tampering, April 2015 to June 2017.
chart.source: Oil ministry, Lok Sabha reply, July 2017.

sections.means: The oil ministry told the Lok Sabha that 101 cases were found, with 44 outlets terminated after joint inspections.
sections.todo: Customers can ask for a filter-paper evaporation test and a density check at any pump, as the post advises.

sections.h2: Karnataka: 11 of 14 petrol samples read above 20% ethanol

chart.title: Eleven of 14 Karnataka samples were above 20%, the highest at 31.2%
chart.sub: Ethanol in petrol, %. State lab results by outlet brand; the oil companies dispute them.
chart.source: Karnataka Department of Legal Metrology, announced 6 November 2026; oil companies' reply.

sections.means: On the state's figures, nine of the 14 samples were above the 21% top of the E20 band and one, at 13.5%, was below it.
sections.todo: A joint retest under the Control Order procedure, with witnesses and retained samples, would settle most of the dispute.

sections.h2: Mileage: the state's 10% loss figure is about five times the energy shortfall

chart.title: At the reported readings the energy loss is 1.9% to 4.1%, against a claimed 10%
chart.sub: Energy per litre lost, %. E20 against pure petrol is shown for scale.
chart.source: Karnataka minister's figures; energy densities as cited in the post.

sections.means: Per litre, the highest reading holds about 4.1% less energy than E20, and the average of the 11 readings above 20% about 1.9% less.
sections.todo: The Rs 62,000 crore figure should be read as a worst-case ceiling rather than an estimate, as the post argues.
